People keep arguing about Democrats versus Republicans while ignoring the incentive structure that shapes both. The real divide isn’t left versus right. It’s establishment versus anyone capable of building a coalition that threatens existing power.

When a candidate starts attracting voters across ideological lines, the political machinery shifts into defense mode. Labels, outrage, identity politics, and media narratives become the performance. The audience argues over the actors while the financial, technology, military, and lobbying interests continue writing the script.

Political theater keeps people emotionally invested in teams. Incentive structures explain outcomes far better than campaign slogans. Follow where the money, debt, and institutional power flow, and the narrative becomes much easier to understand.
